operation.name: rgbcomp
operation.description:
Creates an RGB composition using three independent images, or an LRGB composition using the optional luminance image and three monochrome images or a color image. Result image is called composed_rgb.fit or composed_lrgb.fit unless another name is provided in the optional argument. Another optional argument, -nosum tells Siril not to sum exposure times. This impacts FITS keywords such as LIVETIME and STACKCNT

Uses fixed input references and writes only invocation-owned outputs. Optional argument values are sent only when their use_* control is true; zero is preserved.
operation.syntax:
rgbcomp red green blue [-out=result_filename] [-nosum]
rgbcomp -lum=image { rgb_image | red green blue } [-out=result_filename] [-nosum]

help:
Siril 1.4.4. Creates an RGB composition using three independent images, or an LRGB composition using the optional luminance image and three monochrome images or a color image. Result image is called composed_rgb.fit or composed_lrgb.fit unless another name is provided in the optional argument. Another optional argument, -nosum tells Siril not to sum exposure times. This impacts FITS keywords such as LIVETIME and STACKCNT

Uses fixed input references and writes only invocation-owned outputs. Optional argument values are sent only when their use_* control is true; zero is preserved.



runtime is a JSON object. Supported keys: ini, settings, threads, memory_ratio, output_bits, compression, online, selection, findstar, photometry. Networking starts offline and must be enabled explicitly. Selection is omitted for the whole image or explicitly null to clear it; optional CLI arguments use separate use_* controls. Connect transforms to an explicit export, stacking, or analysis endpoint. Only requested dependencies are executed; previews do not make other branches endpoints. Saved output references identify complete checked files, never preview pixels. See reference/coverage.json and docs/usage.md.
